nom: Lecture 2 — Religion and Politics: Henry VIII to Charles I
cartes: Rise of religious conflicts in Europe
Martin Luther, a German monk, publishes his "95 theses" (start of the Reformation)
Henry VIII is crowned king, at the age of 17
The Pope gives Henry VIII the title "Defender of the Faith" (for fighting Luther's ideas)
Henry VIII wants to divorce Catherine of Aragon
Thomas Cromwell becomes Henry VIII's special adviser (replacing Wolsey)
The majority of the English clergy recognise the authority of the king against the Pope
Act in Restraint of Appeals: the Crown becomes the final authority in religious trials
Henry VIII marries Anne Boleyn and is excommunicated by the Pope
Act of Supremacy: Parliament declares Henry VIII Supreme Head of the Church of England
Henry VIII is recognised King of Ireland by the Irish Parliament
Henry VIII's policy becomes more Protestant (first official English translation of the Bible)
Act for the dissolution of the monasteries
The "Pilgrimage of Grace" (rebellion led by Aske in the North of England) is crushed
Birth of Elizabeth (daughter of Anne Boleyn)
Birth of Edward (son of Jane Seymour)
Mary I ("Bloody Mary"), the first queen to rule England, reigns
Mary I, daughter of Catherine of Aragon (life dates)
Edward VI, Henry VIII's son raised as a Protestant (dates given on the slide)
Reign of Elizabeth I (Church and State)
Elizabeth I, brought up a Protestant, comes to the throne at the age of 25
Act of Supremacy: Elizabeth becomes Supreme Governor of the Church
Act of Uniformity: official doctrine of the Church of England, new Prayer Book
Publication of the Thirty-Nine Articles (doctrine of the Church of England)
Elizabeth I dies without children; James Stuart, king of Scotland, becomes James I of England
Charles I succeeds his father James I
Gunpowder Plot: Guy Fawkes is arrested under the Houses of Parliament
Guy Fawkes is executed for treason
A small group of Puritans sails to America on the Mayflower
Parliament votes the Petition of Right; Charles I dissolves Parliament and rules alone for 11 years
Scottish Puritans (Presbyterians) rebel against Charles I and defeat his army twice
The Civil War breaks out (Parliament's Protestant army attacks the King's army)
Charles I is judged, found guilty of treason and executed
